parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the weight of a metre rule. Carry out the following instructions referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1 You are provided with a 1.0 N load, labelled X .

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text: x and y values present all less than 45 cm

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Place the load X on the rule so that its centre is at d = 5.0 cm from the zero end of the rule as shown in Fig. 1.1. Record the value of d in Table 1.1.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Adjust the position of the rule so that it is as near as possible to being balanced, with the 50.0 cm mark to the right of the pivot.

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Measure, and record in the table, the distance x from the centre of the load X to the pivot.

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Measure, and record in the table, the distance y from the pivot to the 50.0 cm mark on the rule.

parts.label: v
parts.text: (v) Repeat the steps (i) – (iv) using d values of 10.0 cm, 15.0 cm, 20.0 cm and 25.0 cm. Table 1.1 d / cm x / cm y / cm [2]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot the graph of y / cm ( y -axis) against x / cm ( x -axis). You do not need to include the origin (0,0) on your graph. [4]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ..................................................[2]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Calculate the weight W of the metre rule using the equation W = L G , where L = 1.0 N. W = ..................................................[2]
